New in v3: every shape's claim list is hashed (SHA-256 of canonical JSON, sorted keys) and stored in its MetadataSet; one root (SHA-256 over 'uid digest' lines sorted by uid) is stored in the scene head. Root: b3a6e1ac3b237154d06a08a7922e33cc61bac7e495d4fe643f2e4f8f2e594def. The page recomputes all digests with WebCrypto from claims.json: 111 of 111 match; changing one claim's text is caught (110 of 111, skin named, root differs). verify.py does the same offline for both scenes.
S

What this does not give: a hash is not a signature. Whoever edits claims.json can also rewrite the scene digests and the root. It becomes accountable only when the root is held somewhere the editor cannot change (the PR text and the merged commit are the first such places); a keyed signature (Ed25519, Sigstore) is the next step and needs a key policy from the owner.

New in v2: the page can check the scene against the claims. It reads each shape's MetadataSet back out of the running X3D scene and compares grade, FMA id, SNOMED id and claim ids with structures.json: 111 of 111 torso shapes agree. Editing one grade in memory (skin S to C) is caught as 110 of 111, naming the shape. This is a self-consistency check, not a signature: someone who edits both files defeats it.
